story: Arlington Water Utilities in Tarrant County piloted satellite leak detection: an algorithm turns satellite scans into points of interest, and crews with listening gear confirm and repair.

claims.text: Arlington Water Utilities runs a water distribution system with 1,470 miles of water mains.
claims.quote: Arlington Water Utilities is responsible for a water distribution system that includes 1,470 miles of water mains.

claims.text: The city's water department started pilot programs with two satellite leak detection companies, ASTERRA and Paradigm Satellite Leak Detection.
claims.quote: Over the past year, the City of Arlington's water department has initiated pilot programs with two satellite leak detection companies - ASTERRA and Paradigm Satellite Leak Detection.

claims.text: Both companies scan the whole city with Earth-orbiting satellites for underground moisture levels and temperature variations.
claims.quote: Both companies scan the entire City with Earth-orbiting satellites to detect underground moisture levels and temperature variations.

claims.text: ASTERRA's computers combine the satellite data with an algorithm to identify points of interest for investigation.
claims.quote: ASTERRA's computers combine the data from satellites with an algorithm to identify points of interest for investigation

claims.text: The city describes ASTERRA's technology as once used to look for water on Mars.
claims.quote: collaborated with ASTERRA, which uses technology that was once used to look for water on Mars.

claims.text: In 2025 ASTERRA gave the city about 340 potential leak locations.
claims.quote: This year, ASTERRA has provided the City with approximately 340 potential leak locations.

claims.text: Those leads resulted in 34 detected and repaired leaks.
claims.quote: That information resulted in 34 detected and repaired leaks.

claims.text: The city estimates ASTERRA saved $440,800 in lost water costs and 1,130,567 gallons of water.
claims.quote: Overall, ASTERRA saved an estimated, $440,800 in lost water costs and 1,130,567 gallons of water.

claims.text: Across both pilots the city reports almost $500,000 in avoided lost water costs.
claims.quote: with savings of almost $500,000 in avoided lost water costs already reported.

claims.text: Before the satellites, the utility relied on citizens to report water flowing where it should not be.
claims.quote: relied on citizens to report water flowing where it shouldn't be

claims.text: The city's three-person leak detection team places acoustic listening equipment on valves and over distribution lines to triangulate a suspected leak.
claims.quote: the City's three-person leak detection team could place acoustic listening equipment on valves and over distribution lines to triangulate a suspected leak

claims.text: A leak that stayed underground could go unnoticed for weeks or even months.
claims.quote: could go unnoticed for weeks or even months.

claims.text: In July the utility tested a second program, Paradigm.
claims.quote: in July Arlington Water Utilities tested another program, Paradigm

claims.text: Paradigm's team cross-checks the satellite data with a map of the city's valves and hydrants to pinpoint where leaks are coming from.
claims.quote: Paradigm's team cross analyzes it with a map of the City's valves and hydrants to specify exact points where leaks are coming from.

claims.text: ASTERRA uses an algorithm to draw conclusions about leaks, and Paradigm uses people.
claims.quote: The difference is where ASTERRA uses an algorithm to draw conclusions about leaks, Paradigm uses people.

claims.text: In the Paradigm test, 7 of 10 points of interest had leaks.
claims.quote: When we tested Paradigm, 7 out of 10 points of interest had leaks.

claims.text: Paradigm has helped locate 33 city leaks and saved $36,617 in energy costs.
claims.quote: Today Paradigm has helped locate 33 City leaks and saved $36,617 in energy costs.

claims.text: Arlington Water Utilities is evaluating both pilot programs for permanent use.
claims.quote: Arlington Water Utilities is evaluating both pilot programs for permanent use as leak detection tools.

claims.text: The utility's conservation supervisor said satellite programs keep the team from spending entire days searching for leaks.
claims.quote: Satellite programs prevent our team from spending entire days searching for leaks

claims.text: Crews now have data-driven locations to investigate.
claims.quote: Now they have data-driven locations to investigate.

claims.text: The utility's 2025 year-end report says it implemented two new leak detection methods.
claims.quote: Arlington Water Utilities has implemented two new leak detection methods for water conservation

claims.text: Splash is a leak detection dog who uses his sense of smell to detect small amounts of chlorine.
claims.quote: Splash is a leak detection canine who uses his strong sense of smell to detect small amounts of chlorine

claims.text: ASTERRA says its Recover product uses L-band synthetic aperture radar to identify potable water leaks across entire water systems.
claims.quote: L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) to identify potable water leaks across entire water systems.

claims.text: ASTERRA says its algorithms detect the unique dielectric signature of potable water.
claims.quote: detect the unique dielectric signature of potable water

claims.text: ASTERRA says the result targets crew deployment for confirmation and repair.
claims.quote: targeted crew deployment for confirmation and repair.

claims.text: Arlington is a city in Tarrant County.
claims.quote: Precinct 2 includes the cities of Arlington, Benbrook, Crowley, Dalworthington Gardens, Edgecliff Village, Kennedale,

cautions: 340 were potential leak locations, never 340 leaks. 34 were detected and repaired.
Figures are 2025 figures from the city's November 21st, 2025 article. Do not present them as 2026 or as a running total.
Do not add ASTERRA's 34 and Paradigm's 33 into one count.
The dollar figures are city estimates of avoided lost water costs. Paradigm's $36,617 is energy costs.
Both were pilots under evaluation for permanent use. Do not say adopted.
70% is Paradigm's 7 of 10 test, not ASTERRA's hit rate. Do not compute an ASTERRA rate.
Use algorithm when describing the city's words. Radar and the potable water signature are ASTERRA's own description, attribute to the company.
Acoustic listening is how the three-person team pinpoints leaks. Do not claim each satellite lead was confirmed acoustically.
No real person's likeness. The supervisor is not drawn as himself.
